problem:
A sample of an ideal gas is in thermal equilibrium at a temperature of 300 K. The molar mass of the gas is 4 g/mol. Take the molar gas constant to be R = 8.314 J/(mol·K). The sample is in a flask, and a sample of a different gas is in another flask beside it. The two flasks are thermally insulated from each other.

What is the root-mean-square speed of the gas molecules?

sentences.text: Just before the molecular speeds were measured, a heater warmed this gas sample by 100 K.
The gas sample consists of an amount of gas equal to 2 mol.
Before the molecular speeds are measured, a heater warms the other sample by 100 K.
Before the molecular speeds are measured, a heater warms the other sample by a few kelvin.
Before the molecular speeds are measured, a heater warms this gas sample by 100 K.
In an earlier experiment, a heater warmed this gas sample by 100 K.

problem:
A ray of light in a medium of refractive index 1 meets a flat interface with a second medium of refractive index 1.5. The angle of incidence, measured from the normal, is 40 degrees. A camera on a tripod films the interface.

What is the angle of refraction, measured from the normal?

sentences.text: Before the refraction was observed, the laser that produces the ray was tilted until the angle of incidence had grown by 11°.
The camera on the tripod is then tilted a little farther from the vertical to keep the ray in view.
The ray is then tilted until its angle of incidence at the interface has grown by 11°.
In an earlier experiment, the laser that produces the ray was tilted until the angle of incidence had grown by a little.
